items.headline: RBI maintains repo rate at 5.25%, upgrades FY27 GDP outlook to 6.7%
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept its benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, maintaining a 'Neutral' policy stance. The RBI upgraded its FY27 GDP growth outlook to 6.7% from 6.6% and lowered its FY27 CPI inflation forecast to 5.0% from 5.1%, though retail inflation is projected to rise to 4.5% in July 2026.

items.headline: Cabinet approves GOBARdhan Scheme; Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 proposed
items.summary: The Cabinet has approved the ₹23,731 crore GOBARdhan Scheme. Additionally, the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes a significant overhaul of the corporate statute, including a single-bench framework under the NCLT for streamlined merger approvals.

items.headline: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East push crude prices higher, global markets mixed
items.summary: Global market sentiment is influenced by ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerns around shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has led to Brent crude futures rising above $83 a barrel. This is a negative for India. Most Asian markets saw declines, and US markets traded mixed or lower. However, foreign investors bought a net of $1.3 billion in August so far, adding to $2.1 billion purchased in July.

items.headline: Indian market mixed; Telecom, Metal sectors face pressure, Oil & Gas, Banking see buying
items.summary: On Thursday, the Indian stock market ended on a mixed note, with the Nifty 50 largely unchanged while the Sensex posted a modest gain. Sectoral indices experienced mixed movements, with telecommunication and metal sectors facing selling pressure, while oil & gas and banking sectors witnessed buying.

items.headline: Experts identify sectors resilient to inflation, others under pressure
items.summary: Experts suggest that FMCG, healthcare, banks, and select agriculture-linked businesses are better positioned to handle moderate inflation, while auto, consumer durables, real estate, and aviation sectors might face pressure.

items.headline: RBI allows banks to finance acquisitions; IBC Amendment Act, 2026 streamlines distressed dealmaking
items.summary: Effective July 1, 2026, RBI allows Indian banks to finance up to 75% of acquisition value for eligible non-financial corporate borrowers. Additionally, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) (Amendment) Act, 2026, introduces a creditor-initiated insolvency resolution process, streamlining distressed dealmaking.
